points: There is no referee, so both sides are the referee. Each player judges their own side of the net.
There is no appeal and no replay of a point that was already decided.
A solution both sides agree to in good faith stands, even if it later turns out to be wrong.
Argue before the next point, not after the match.
Nobody except the players is involved: no spectators, captains, coaches, club staff or players on other courts.
One exception: captains may be asked onto the court to explain the timed procedure in the last 20 minutes.

questions.q: In a league match with no referee, who makes the calls on your side of the net?
options: You, and your partner in doubles
Whoever had the best view, on either side
The home team captain
Both sides must agree on every call
questions.why: Each player is the only judge of their own side of the net.

questions.q: You and your opponents disagreed, talked it over and agreed in good faith how to settle it. After the match you learn the agreement did not follow the rules. What happens?
options: The result stands
The point is replayed at the next match
The match result is cancelled
The team that lost the point can appeal
questions.why: A solution both sides agree to in good faith stands, even if it later turns out to be wrong.

questions.q: A spectator with a clear view offers to tell you if the ball was in. What do you do?
options: Say no thanks. Only the players make calls
Accept it if both sides agree to listen
Accept it if the spectator is neutral
Ask a player on the next court instead
questions.why: Nobody except the players is involved in a match. Do not ask others, and do not accept a call that is offered.

questions.q: When may players ask a captain to come onto the court during a match?
options: Only to explain the timed procedure in the last 20 minutes
To settle a line call that both sides argue about
To settle a dispute about the score
Any time both sides agree to it
questions.why: Captains stay out of the match. The only exception is the timed procedure in the last 20 minutes.

questions.q: You think something went wrong on a point. When is the time to raise it?
options: Right away, before the next point is played
At the next changeover
At the end of the set
After the match, through the captains
questions.why: Argue before the next point, not after the match. A point that was decided is not replayed later.

questions.q: Your opponent calls your shot out. You are sure it was in. What are your options?
options: Accept it. It is their side and their call
Ask for the point to be replayed
Ask someone watching to decide
Take the point, since you saw it clearly
questions.why: Each player is the only judge of their own side. There is no appeal and no replay of a decided point.
